intro.text: The Transit Hub never sleeps. Trains of cars roll through, each car knowing only which car comes next.
Quack. That is a linked list. If you lose the pointer to the next car, the rest of the train is gone for good. Order matters.

mid.text: Trains are sorted. Now the parcel lockers: thousands of parcels, and customers want theirs in seconds.
Quack. A hash function turns a name into a locker number. When two parcels share a locker, we chain them like train cars.

outro.text: Linked lists for flexible growth, hash tables for fast lookup. Everything has a trade-off.
Quack. Next the Library, where Python makes all of this a lot shorter.

games.title: Couple the Cars
games.instructions: Click the pointer steps in the right order. Pick wrongly and cars get lost.

wrong.blue->next = pink: Too early! Nothing points at green anymore, so Green and Gold are lost (a leak). Attach pink to the rest first.
wrong.free(blue): That frees the car you're attaching to.

rounds.explain: Pink grabbed the rest of the train before blue let go of it.

wrong.free(green): Freed too soon: green->next is now garbage, so Gold is lost. Bypass green first.
wrong.green->next = NULL: That cuts Gold off instead of bypassing green.

rounds.explain: Pink skips green, then green is safely freed.

rounds.prompt: Add silver as the new head of the train.

wrong.head = silver: Too early: nothing remembers the old head, so the whole train is lost.
wrong.red->next = silver: That loops the train: Red leads to Silver, which leads to Red.

rounds.explain: Silver points at the old head first, then becomes the head.

games.title: Parcel Lockers
games.instructions: hash(name) = number of letters mod 5. Click the right locker for each parcel; collisions chain together. Then find a few parcels.
